violations.issue: This is a psychiatry MCQ testing diagnostic/treatment knowledge, not medication management dosing/safety
violations.suggested_fix: This item should be evaluated by psychiatric expert, not medication management expert. Content focuses on depression diagnosis (DSM-5 criteria), SSRI selection, treatment-resistant depression, elderly dosing principles, postpartum depression - not specific medication dosing, PBS compliance, or drug interactions requiring pharmacology expertise.

suggestions: Route to psychiatry expert or clinical-documentation-expert for evaluation
If medication-specific evaluation needed, extract only medication-related content (e.g., 'sertraline 50mg daily' from options) and evaluate that in isolation
strengths: MCQ uses Australian medication names (sertraline, escitalopram, mirtazapine, venlafaxine) consistently
Mentions appropriate SSRI dosing principles for elderly (start low, titrate slowly)
agent_evaluations.notes: This MCQ tests psychiatric diagnosis and treatment selection, not medication management. While it mentions SSRIs and dosing principles, the core competency being assessed is psychiatric diagnosis (major depressive disorder criteria) and first-line treatment selection. A psychiatry expert would be better suited to evaluate clinical accuracy of depression management. Medication management expert would only evaluate if the question specifically tested PBS compliance, renal dosing calculations, drug interactions, or polypharmacy management - which this item does not.

suggestions: URGENT: Add SAFE-T framework assessment to all suicide/depression MCQs (Specific plan, Access to means, Feelings, Earlier attempts, Threat)

Add C-SSRS category classification to suicide risk MCQs
Include least restrictive alternative principle in all involuntary admission scenarios
Add Aboriginal Mental Health Liaison Officer offer in appropriate cases
Specify risk stratification (high/medium/low) with clear criteria
Add safety planning components (warning signs, coping strategies, crisis contacts)
